newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Justice announces indictment in ADM probe.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Justice announces indictment in ADM probe.

text.p: A federal grand jury in Chicago Tuesday indicted three former top Archer Daniels Midland Co. executives for conspiring to fix lysine prices, the Justice Department said.

It said the indictment named Michael Andreas, the former executive vice president and son of ADM's chairman; former Vice President Terrance Wilson, who headed up the corn-processing unit; and Mark Whitacre, a fired ADM executive who had been an FBI informant in the case.

The Justice Department also announced that Cheil Jedang Ltd., based in Seoul, South Korea, agreed to plead guilty and pay a $1.25 million fine for participating in the conspiracy to fix prices of lysine, a feed additive for livestock.

Apart from the three former ADM executives, the Justice Department said the grand jury also indicted Kazutoshi Yamada, a managing director of Ajinomoto Co. Inc. The Japanese company previously entered a guilty plea in the investigation.

In October, Archer Daniels Midland agreed to plead guilty to two counts of federal charges of price fixing in the sale of agricultural products and to pay record fines totalling $100 million. The indictment of ADM's former executives had been expected since then.
The Justice Department said its antitrust investigation into the lysine, citric acid and high-fructose corn syrup markets continues.

"These charges should signal to business executives, both at home and abroad, that we will vigorously pursue individuals involved in international cartels, wherever they are," Acting Assistant Attorney General Joel Klein said in a statement.

The indictment charged the defendants conspired with ADM, three previously charged companies, and other unnamed corporate and individual co-conspirators to suppress competition in the worldwide lysine market, a $600 million a year industry.
The indictment charged the defendants with fixing prices and allocating sales volumes for three years, starting in June 1992.
The Justice Department said the indictment specifically charged the defendants and co-conspirators:
-- agreed to charge lysine prices at agreed-upon levels and to increase those prices accordingly.
-- agreed to allocate among the companies the volume of lysine to be sold by each firm.
-- issued price announcements and price quotations in accordance with the agreements.
-- participated in meetings and conversations for the purpose of monitoring and enforcing adherence to the agreed-upon prics and sales volumes.

Besides ADM, Ajinomoto and now Cheil Jedang, other companies which agreed to plead guilty and cooperate in the probe have been Kyowa Hakko Kogyo Co Ltd and Sewon America, a unit of the South Korean-based Sewon Co Ltd.
The individuals who were indicted face a maximum prison term of three years if convicted. In addition, they face possible fines.
